findings.evidence: features/004-decision-skill/004-decision-skill-prd.md:R5 — 'Before writing, the skill identifies the most-recently-written existing entry and verifies it contains exactly the five canonical bold-prefixed fields...'. R5 says 'most-recently-written existing entry' but does not define what 'most-recently-written' means: is it (a) the last entry in file order (the entry immediately preceding the file's final `---` separator), (b) the entry with the most recent `**Date:**` field value, or (c) the most recently committed/modified entry per `git blame`? The three definitions can disagree — entries in the worked-example file are in chronological order today but a future user might insert an entry mid-file (against the append-only rule, but it could happen by mistake) and the `**Date:**` value would be older than the literal-last entry. AC-4 inherits the same ambiguity: 'when the most-recently-written existing entry... has additional fields'. Without a defined operational meaning for 'most-recently-written', a fresh agent implementing R5 cannot tell which entry to check, and the Goal-Driven binary-test fails: AC-4 cannot fire deterministically.
findings.claim: Unstated assumption — R5's trigger condition rests on 'most-recently-written' without defining which of three possible interpretations applies. Think-Before-Coding line: 'state assumptions explicitly.' The three interpretations (file-order-last, date-field-most-recent, git-blame-most-recent) produce different entries to check in a file whose entries are not strictly chronological. The implementation needs the canonical reading order — file order (top-to-bottom) is what a future Phase 3 `/insights` consumer will see and what matches the file's append-only convention — but the PRD does not state this, leaving R5's trigger non-deterministic.
findings.proposed_change: Edit R5 to state the canonical reading order explicitly: 'Before writing, the skill identifies the most-recently-written existing entry — defined as the **last entry in file order** (i.e. the entry immediately preceding the file's final `---` separator, or the only entry in the file). The skill does NOT use date-based ordering for this check; file order is the canonical reading order and matches what a future Phase 3 consumer will see.' Update AC-4 to reference 'the last entry in file order' explicitly, and update its warning text to name file-order: *"Last entry in file order ('{title}', line {N}) contains {description of drift} — continuing with canonical schema"*. This closes the unstated-assumption gap and makes R5 + AC-4 deterministic.

findings.evidence: features/004-decision-skill/004-decision-skill-prd.md:R9 + AC-8 — R9 says the skill performs 'a minimal parse before writing — read the file, verify it ends with either (a) the file's preamble alone followed by `---` (no entries yet) or (b) a complete entry — H2 title, all five canonical fields in order, trailing `---` separator.' AC-8 says 'when `admin/decision-log.md` exists but its tail does not match...'. The parse is described as 'tail-only' but the tail extent is not bounded — does the skill read the entire file and check the last N lines, or only read the last N bytes? For a long-lived project with hundreds of entries, the file could be megabytes; reading the entire file is wasteful. For a short file, reading only the tail might miss the preamble-only case (the preamble is at the head, not the tail).
findings.claim: Missing tradeoff articulation — R9's parse strategy is unstated as a tradeoff. The PRD says 'minimal parse' but does not name the read strategy (full-file read vs. last-N-lines read vs. last-N-bytes read). The corner case — a fresh file with the preamble only and no entries — requires the parser to recognise the preamble's presence, which requires reading the head not the tail. Conflating 'preamble-only-no-entries' with 'tail check' is the unstated tradeoff: the parser actually has to handle two read modes (head-read for the preamble-only case, tail-read for the existing-entries case) OR read the whole file in both cases.
findings.proposed_change: Add a sentence to R9 stating the read strategy: 'The parse reads the entire file — `admin/decision-log.md` is bounded in practice (decisions are dozens per project, not thousands), so a full-file read is operationally cheap and the simplest correct shape. The parse then checks (i) head: file starts with the canonical preamble; (ii) tail: file ends with either the preamble's `---` separator (no entries yet) or a complete entry + `---` separator.' This names the tradeoff explicitly (full-file read chosen over partial-read for simplicity, with the practical-size argument as justification) and makes both edge cases (preamble-only and existing-entries) explicit.
